title: Two New England beach towns to visit before the summer ends
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Harwich, Massachusetts was voted the best town on Cape Cod by Boston.com readers, known for its beaches and oyster specials.
Chach Restaurant in Provincetown will close on November 3 after 21 years, announced by owners Viola Briseño and Sharon Bowes.
Ogunquit, Maine, named New England's best beach town, offers scenic views and attractions, ideal for summer visits.

title: Diver dies in incident off Cape Cod
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 72-year-old man died in a diving incident off Cape Cod on Wednesday afternoon.
The search for the missing diver involved firefighting marine units and U.S. Coast Guard aerial support.
Authorities located the diver around 5:30 p.m.; he was pronounced dead at Sesuit Harbor.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues after graphic testimony about children’s autopsies
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continues with emotional testimonies about her children's autopsies and causes of death.
Clancy, claiming postpartum mental illness, has admitted to the January 2023 strangulation of her three children in Duxbury.
Defense attorney raised objections during Dr. Barbara Olson's testimony about asphyxia and brain damage in Clancy's children.

title: Rhode Island beach house with water views on both sides — can you guess the price?
author: Emily Turner
bullets: The Westerly, Rhode Island beach house was built in 1987 with contemporary cottage style.
The property includes 2,724 square feet, 3 bedrooms, and 3 full baths.
Annual taxes for the property are $11,125 as of 2025.

title: 5 best new restaurant openings and dining updates in Boston (August 13, 2026)
author: Nathan Tavares
bullets: First Crush, a natural wine bar by Gabrielle Malina, opens mid-September in Somerville's Union Square.
Johnny Boy transitions from a Filipino-inspired sandwich popup to a permanent restaurant in Fort Point this fall.
Jūni, a sushi bar by Chris Chung and Kenny Leung, is now open with ten seats in Quincy Center.

title: 3 concerning trends from Red Sox’ 5-game losing skid
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Boston Red Sox have entered a five-game losing streak, despite a prior 44-day period with only five losses.
The Red Sox struggle with offense, averaging 2.8 runs per game in the losing streak, and a .119 average with runners in scoring position.
Boston's bullpen performance has declined, with key relievers like Tyron Guerrero and Aroldis Chapman allowing crucial runs.

title: An Easton church has been converted to a $1.3m home
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: A former church at 16 Williams St., Easton, converted into a home, is listed for $1.3 million.
The 5,730 sq. ft. residence has four bedrooms, three and a half bathrooms, and features original church design elements.
Key features include a Viking-equipped kitchen, a great room with stained glass, and a primary suite with a spa-like bathroom.

title: Blue Jays erupt for 5 runs in the eighth to beat Red Sox 6-4, extend Boston’s skid to 5
author: The Associated Press
bullets: Blue Jays score five runs in the eighth inning, defeating the Red Sox 6-4 in Toronto.
Willson Contreras hits his 24th home run; Red Sox extend losing streak to five games.
Kazuma Okamoto and Myles Straw deliver key hits in Toronto's eighth-inning rally.

title: Allston-Brighton residents divided over future of Jackson Mann Community Center, survey shows
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Survey shows Allston-Brighton residents divided on whether Jackson Mann site should include housing, a school, or both.
553 residents participated in the survey: 190 prefer housing, 171 prefer a school, and 124 prefer both options.
Mayor Michelle Wu will decide on the center’s future by the end of the year after further community feedback.

title: Tour the Patriots’ new 160,000-square-foot training facility
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The New England Patriots unveiled their new 160,000-square-foot training facility next to Gillette Stadium.
The New Balance Athletics Center includes a 15,000-square-foot weight room and a 10,500-square-foot virtual reality room.
The facility features a restaurant-style dining room, hydrotherapy room, and a player’s lounge with entertainment amenities.
